patch.value: pm-changelog consumes a truncated `pm list-all` answer as if it were complete

readPmItems shells out to pm list-all --json and takes .items via parsePmItemsJson without consulting the answer's completeness receipt. Under pm-cli 2026.8.14 the default output budget returned 10 of 682 workspace items with truncated=true, and pm-changelog generated a changelog missing most entries while reporting success. truncated can still go true under an output budget and completeness.status can go partial when item documents are unreadable, so the read itself must refuse those answers instead of generating from half a workspace.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Wired refusal signals at the list-all read (src/generator.ts readPmItems -> parseListAllItemsJson): truncated===true, has_more===true, completeness.status!=='complete' (a missing or non-object receipt counts as incomplete), omission_receipt.has_omissions===true. The new typed IncompleteListAllError names every tripped signal plus count vs total, and readPmItems propagates it so the CLI exits non-zero instead of writing a changelog from half the history. next_cursor is deliberately NOT followed: no paging consumer here, refusing loudly is the contract. Also exact-pinned @unbrained/pm-cli to 2026.8.15 in devDependencies (^2026.8.11 before) and peerDependencies (>=2026.8.3 before). Revert-proof: with parseListAllItemsJson reverted to the permissive parsePmItemsJson behavior, nine regression tests fail, e.g. 'AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Missing expected exception: the refusal must name the truncated signal and the counts'; only the happy-path test still passes.

author: claude-agent

value.author: claude-agent
value.text:
Rebase onto main plus the fleet compatibility convention (PR #143).

The branch went DIRTY after Dependabot PRs #140 and #141 merged to main, conflicting on `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. Resolved by taking each side's own contribution: the branch's EXACT `@unbrained/pm-cli` pin at 2026.8.15 (the point of this PR) and main's newer `pm-ops` 2026.8.10 (the merged bump). One commit dropped as already upstream.

While resolving, three compatibility declarations were brought in line with the convention the rest of the fleet converged on today:

- `peerDependencies` was the EXACT `2026.8.15`. Corrected to the lower-bound `>=2026.8.15`: an exact peer pin makes every later CLI patch a peer conflict for consumers under strict peer resolution, turning a compatibility statement into a lockstep release dependency. Reviewers raised this independently on pm-beads, pm-brief and pm-context.
- `manifest.json` `pm_min_version` was still `2026.8.3`, three releases below the peer floor, so the pm host would have loaded this package on a CLI that predates the completeness receipt it depends on. Corrected to 2026.8.15 and verified against the SDK gate: 2026.8.14 now fails with `pm_min_version_unmet`, 2026.8.15 and 2027.1.1 pass.
- The lockfile root metadata was regenerated so `npm ci` sees a consistent manifest and lockfile.

Two regression tests added, matching those now in pm-beads, pm-brief, pm-context and pm-linear: one binds `pm_min_version` to the peer floor and asserts the dev pin is exact rather than a range, the other runs the SDK host gate against the manifest bytes on disk so a floor moved into a field the gate does not read fails loudly instead of shipping inert. That second case is not hypothetical — it is exactly how pm-context and pm-linear ended up with no enforced floor at all.

release:check green including changelog:check.

message: Record the rebase and the compatibility-convention alignment
